title: Starting — Engine Start, Dry Motoring and Starter Duty Limits

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew procedure for engine start and dry motoring, including the starter duty cycle, the extended motoring run used for core conditioning and the actions after an aborted start.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the flight crew procedure for engine start and for dry motoring, and states the starter duty limits that govern how many attempts may be made.
sections.description: The engine is started with air from the auxiliary power unit, from the other engine or from a ground cart. The starter is a duty limited item: it may be run for a maximum period and must then be allowed to cool for a stated interval before the next attempt, and the number of consecutive attempts is limited. Dry motoring is used to clear a wet start, to cool the core before a start and, on some operators, as a routine core conditioning run before the first flight of the day. The extended motoring run used for that purpose is longer than the run used to clear a wet start and it counts fully against the starter duty cycle. Crews should treat a motoring run as a start cycle for the purpose of counting attempts. An audible leak from the starter area at the end of a long motoring run should be reported even if no alert is generated.
sections.crew_procedure: Confirm the air supply pressure before selecting the start. Observe the starter duty limits and the cooling interval between attempts, counting every motoring run as an attempt. After an aborted start, motor the engine for the period given in the procedure before a further attempt. Do not exceed the maximum motoring duration in an attempt to clear a hot start; shut down, allow the cooling interval and report it. Report any audible leak from the starter area at the end of a long motoring run, with the duration of the run.

type_data.crew_action: Observe the starter duty limits and count every motoring run as an attempt. Report an audible leak after a long run.
